title: Welcome to the Real World: How You Live in Your Own Simulation of Reality — and How We Can Still Share a World. A Theory of Persistence, Emergence, Learning, and Correctable Intelligence
description: Evolution by Emergence is an open research corpus and machine-auditable candidate architecture for resource-constrained cumulative evolution. Version v23.3 keeps everything in v23.2: CORE.md opens with what a functional world model is and follows one model of learning, read as a network, in eight steps, and formalization/ebe-core/EbECore.lean audits 96 machine-checked results; no Lean module is added. It adds four pieces of work outside the core, each labelled where it stands. A working note compares two ways to charge for misfit in learning, counting wrong worlds and the log-loss of the actual world; an outside review reproduced every number, its corrections were accepted, and it judged that nothing mathematical is added. A feasibility study of the Ten Verbs Hypothesis, in one model written by the assistant, asks whether a task can tell ten proposed functions of learning apart; four outside reviews are kept, and it is closed as a feasibility study with a brief for an independent experiment. A working note reads OpenAI's published base-model perplexity curve through two of the author's January 2026 preprints on functional information, states five predictions with what would count against each, reports that one already fails a first check, and designs a study on open model checkpoints that has not been run. In the Yang–Mills working space, an attempt to prove that a quantity D(p) never decreases, which would make a crossing probability nondecreasing, gives a reformulation, two lemmas and a failed route, and no proof; the space still contains no mass-gap result. Retained from v23.2: the working note on what one turn of learning consists of, the creed's two draft sections and the legal concept note. No human expert has reviewed the additions of this release. DIALOGUE.md records how the author and an AI assistant build the model together, now in 54 entries. The release title uses ‘simulation of reality’ to mean the internal model through which a system experiences and acts in the world, not a claim that reality itself is simulated. Formal verification establishes implications under explicit premises; empirical, causal, political and normative interpretations remain open.
